key_insight: MFG trains an LLM to improve molecules over multiple turns using feedback, making multi-objective optimization more progressive and feedback-aware.
clinical_relevance: This could help generate drug-like candidates that better balance potency-related properties while preserving structural similarity, a useful step in early therapeutic discovery.
method: Built a reinforcement learning framework on top of GeLLM³O for iterative molecular optimization.
Added a feedback vector encoding property gains and similarity to the starting molecule.
Used a feedback-aligned reward to encourage improvement across successive turns.
evidence_signal: Across ten multi-objective optimization tasks, GeLLM³O-MFG achieved an average similarity-constrained success rate of 81.50%, compared with 70.81% for the base model.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality of feedback signals and reward design, so performance may be sensitive to task setup and may not directly translate to experimental drug candidates.
paper_title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
